search_log: Searched 'Knife of Dreams Robert Jordan excerpt', 'first chapter', 'When Last Sounds', and 'Embers Falling on Dry Grass'; opened the Tor/Macmillan and Google Books pages, but neither exposed a usable prose excerpt to the crawler, and unauthorized full-text transcriptions were excluded.

Searched the verified title with 'point of view', 'third person', 'narrator', and 'narrated by'; opened the GradeSaver literary-elements page, the Tar Valon chapter-by-chapter POV list, and an independent review explicitly identifying third person with multiple viewpoints.

Searched Wheel of Time narrative technique with 'third person limited', 'omniscient', and scholarly-analysis terms; opened Writing Excuses transcripts in which Brandon Sanderson describes the series-wide third-person zoom-out and limited-viewpoint structure, plus a doctoral thesis and other analyses for corroboration.

Searched the title with 'epistolary', 'diary', 'frame narrative', 'alternating narration', 'first person', and 'second person'; results instead consistently described rotating character POV sections, with no credible evidence of sustained first- or second-person base narration.
person_note: The controlling narration is third person, chiefly rotating third-person-limited focalization among Mat, Perrin, Elayne, Rand, Egwene, and many other characters, with occasional omniscient establishing narration. The sustained Goodreads scenes for Perrin and Mat and the interior passages about several women independently expose this structure. First-person and second-person forms in the sample occur in dialogue, direct thought, song, prophecy, or generic maxims rather than autonomous base sections. Web research explicitly identifies third-person narration and documents character viewpoints across the entire book; no credible frame, epistolary structure, or sustained first- or second-person strand was found. The only limitation is that the authorized publisher excerpt was not accessible, but the agreement between diagnostic quotations, an authoritative series-level craft description, and multiple title-specific structural sources supports high confidence.
